purpose: Manufacturer-verified Tenstorrent Blackhole PCIe accelerator and TT-QuietBox 2 workstation records for local/on-premise AI and LLM inference, preserving current pricing, availability, exact part numbers, software paths, and documented uncertainty around aggregate bandwidth and system power.

hardware.architecture: Tenstorrent Blackhole Tensix Processor; 120 Tensix cores, 16 SiFive X280 Big RISC-V cores, 180 MB SRAM
hardware.external_power: 12V-2x6 (12+4-pin); ATX 3.1 or newer PSU recommended by manufacturer
quantization_compatibility: Native low-precision formats include FP8, BLOCKFP8, BLOCKFP4, BLOCKFP2 and INT8; model-format compatibility depends on Tenstorrent compiler/runtime support
hardware.model_size_practicality: 28GB raw accelerator memory is well suited to 7B-14B quantized models and many models in the roughly 20B class. Some larger quantized models may fit tightly depending on context, KV cache and runtime overhead; capacity alone does not imply validated model support.
hardware.off_grid_suitability: low_to_moderate; 300W board power plus host overhead is substantial, although compact single-card deployment avoids a multi-GPU server
hardware.efficiency_notes: Specification-derived memory capacity is about 0.093 GB/W and memory bandwidth about 1.49 GB/s/W at the 300W board-power ceiling. These are not tokens-per-joule measurements.
source_caveats: Current product and technical documentation specify 120 Tensix cores. Some older Tenstorrent lesson pages still mention 140; newer firmware/software documentation indicates the exposed configuration was standardized to 120.
No independent cross-platform LLM tokens/s result is used here; software optimization and model coverage remain workload/version dependent.

hardware.architecture: Tenstorrent Blackhole Tensix Processor; 120 Tensix cores, 16 SiFive X280 Big RISC-V cores, 180 MB SRAM
hardware.external_power: 12V-2x6 (12+4-pin); ATX 3.1 or newer PSU recommended by manufacturer
networking: 4x passive QSFP-DD 800G ports for Blackhole-to-Blackhole links
quantization_compatibility: Native low-precision formats include FP8, BLOCKFP8, BLOCKFP4, BLOCKFP2 and INT8; model-format compatibility depends on Tenstorrent compiler/runtime support
hardware.model_size_practicality: 32GB raw accelerator memory supports a strong single-card 7B-20B quantized tier. The p150 fabric can link multiple cards and pool capacity for larger models; Tenstorrent documents multi-card Blackhole configurations for 70B-class workloads. Real fit and performance depend on model/runtime support, tensor parallelism, context and KV cache.
hardware.off_grid_suitability: low_to_moderate; 300W per card plus host and networking overhead, but scalable capacity can be built incrementally rather than with a full datacenter chassis
hardware.efficiency_notes: Specification-derived ratios are about 0.107 GB/W and 1.71 GB/s/W at 300W TBP. Multi-card system efficiency must include host, fabric and cooling power.
source_caveats: Four 800G QSFP-DD ports are dedicated Blackhole-to-Blackhole links and should not be treated as general Ethernet NIC bandwidth.
Current product and hardware documentation specify 120 Tensix cores per Blackhole chip; older lesson material may show 140.

hardware.architecture: Four Tenstorrent Blackhole chips; 480 total Tensix cores; two liquid-cooled p300c cards
hardware.memory_bandwidth_note: Tenstorrent's current QuietBox 2 guide describes 1,024 GB/s per p300c card and the welcome page summarizes 2 TB/s across the four-chip workstation. Aggregate bandwidth is topology-dependent and should not be interpreted as a single flat 2 TB/s memory pool.
hardware.accelerator_cards: 2x Blackhole p300c (TC-03007), 2 chips/card; p300c is not sold separately
hardware.system_power_caveat: Tenstorrent's specification table lists 1500W peak power consumption while accompanying operating guidance says the system draws up to about 1300W at peak load; neither is a measured LLM inference average.
quantization_compatibility: Blackhole native low-precision formats include FP8, BLOCKFP8/BLOCKFP4/BLOCKFP2 and INT8; supported model packages depend on Tenstorrent software/model releases
hardware.model_size_practicality: 128GB total accelerator memory is a practical 70B-class local-inference capacity tier when supported by the Tenstorrent stack. Tenstorrent explicitly positions QuietBox 2 for 32B and 70B scale and ships Qwen3-32B preloaded. Larger models may require unsupported partitioning/offload or additional systems.
hardware.off_grid_suitability: very_low; compact for its accelerator capacity but approximately 1.3-1.5kW peak system demand makes it unsuitable for most small off-grid installations
hardware.efficiency_notes: Using the 1500W published peak figure gives a conservative capacity ratio of about 0.085 GB accelerator memory/W at system peak. Do not infer tokens/joule without workload-specific measured wall power.
source_caveats: p300c is an internal QuietBox 2 card and is not sold separately.
Aggregate 2 TB/s bandwidth is distributed across two dual-chip p300c cards; topology and workload mapping affect realized bandwidth.
Published power values are system peak/input guidance, not a measured LLM inference average.
